body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31929

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/2169

## What changed

- Derive `cur_expert_start` from the token counts already held in registers instead of reloading the just-written global prefix array without a CTA barrier.
- Add a failing-before invariant regression and GPU reference cases for zero counts, padded tails, block sizes 32/64/128, and non-power-of-two expert counts.
- Record compiler, GPU, and limitation evidence in `reports/j-a22f70b60735/`.

## Evidence and reproduction

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a22f70b60735/triton-cache-final /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a22f70b60735/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_ep_scatter.py
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a22f70b60735/venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_ep_scatter.py
```

The focused suite passed 5/5 cases on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950). Baseline generated gfx950 ISA preserved a global prefix store followed by a global reload with no barrier; post-fix TTIR contains no `cur_expert_start` reload. A 200-launch guarded stress/reference probe passed before and after, so the intermittent illegal access itself was not observed on gfx950.

## Limitations

The report used NVIDIA H20/CUDA, but this job supplied one AMD gfx950 GPU. No H20, model weights, or multi-node DeepEP setup was available, so the exact PTX scheduling, full-model illegal access, and downstream CPU recv timeout were not reproduced. No native C++/FlyDSL code changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
